Intensive and extensive infection of leaflets, rachis, petioles and stem, exhibiting brownish to purple black lesions with whitish fungal growth on underside of the leaves, showing conidiophores and conidia (zoosporangia) under the microscope; conidia measuring 20-38μ x 12-23 μ in diameter. Conidial and mycelial suspension in water produced the typical symptoms of the disease at 20°C. In later stages potato tubers were also found to be infected.
The image shows a potato plant infected by Rhizoctonia canker, with visible cankers on the stem and tubers.

Panicle reduced in size and thickened, floral branches bunched together in cone-like or black mass structures. No fruit setting. Moderately reduced size of panicles allowing some floral branches to separate out. Multiple smaller compact cones instead of a single large one. Vegetative leaves appear on the panicle intermingled with small cones. Malformed cones in previous years produce malformed and healthy types of inflorescence next year. Diseased flowers have disproportion of staminate and hermaphroditic flowers, and unisexual staminate flowers are exclusively found.
